title: Root-normalized derived finite quotient comparisons
statement: Fix the coefficient lines of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, and the completed shifted root complexes $C_{X,d}$ of [def-sf-orientation-integral-line-comparisons]. For $m\ge0$ the finite quotient complex is the single complex of $A_{E,m+1}(d)$ in degree $-2d$. Its derived quotient comparison $\mathrm{red}_{m+1}(QC_{X,d})\cong Q(A_{E,m+1}(d)[2d])$ is the unique family whose scalar-adjunction transpose is induced by the ordinary quotient of root powers: completed coefficient projection at zero, the scalar-extension unit of the first root line at one, and tensor multiplication at higher powers. Every ordinary arrow is normalized on all local pure root tensors. Use exact restriction, its single-complex comparison and its derived factors for the transpose. Positive quotient finiteness is the existing coefficient quotient theorem. The definition contains the actual uniquely normalized comparison and no arbitrary quotient isomorphism.
